title: arxiv_2101.02702v3
universal_lens: The universal lens unifies multi-object tracking and sports intelligence via a set-prediction operator. By mapping spatio-temporal trajectories to an attention-based manifold, the framework treats identity persistence as a continuous state-transition problem, eliminating discrete graph optimizations in favor of differentiable, global feature alignment across sequential frames. Ground truth track identity mappings Kt ⊂ K and Kt-1 ⊂ K define temporal consistency via intersection Kt ∩ Kt-1 and set differences Kt-1 \ Kt, Kt \ Kt-1 for match, occlusion, and new object identification.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps track queries to Bayesian posterior updates over player identities. Static object queries act as priors for new entrants, while autoregressive track queries refine conformal prediction sets. Global frame-level features provide the likelihood, ensuring robust identity discrimination under occlusion without explicit motion models. Bayesian belief updates on track identity sets Kt, Kt-1 encode posterior probabilities over object persistence and emergence using conformal predictive distributions.
gse_mapping: In GSE, situational reasoning is modeled through the evolution of track queries. Each query represents a dynamic agent whose state transitions are governed by encoder-decoder attention. This allows real-time trajectory forecasting and identity preservation, directly translating visual attention into actionable game-state vectors. State transitions in track query embeddings map to frame-to-frame identity propagation through hard assignment Kt ∩ Kt-1 and cost-minimized mappings Kt \ Kt-1.

primitives.name: MOT Set Prediction Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: We formulate this task as a frame-to-frame set prediction problem and introduce TrackFormer, an end-to-end trainable MOT approach based on an encoder-decoder Transformer architecture.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Frame: dimensionless temporal index; Set: collection of bounding boxes (meters); Identity: dimensionless categorical label.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes objects can be represented as a fixed-size set per frame and that global context is sufficient for association.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the number of objects exceeds the maximum capacity of static object queries or under extreme, prolonged total occlusion.

layer2.mapping: Maps the detection-and-association pipeline to a single differentiable optimization surface, mirroring how GSI collapses multi-agent belief states into unified probability distributions.
layer2.telemetry: Multi-Object Tracking Accuracy (MOTA) and IDF1 scores.

primitives.name: Autoregressive Track Query Evolution
primitives.verbatim_quote: The Transformer decoder initializes new tracks from static object queries and autoregressively follows existing tracks in space and time with the conceptually new and identity preserving track queries.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Track Query: latent vector (dimensionless); Space: Euclidean coordinates (pixels/meters); Time: discrete sequence index.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes temporal continuity of object existence and that past track states inform future positions via attention weights.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if an object undergoes a sudden, discontinuous teleportation-like movement that violates the learned spatio-temporal attention priors.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's state-transition kernel, where the track query acts as the hidden state propagating through the Markov chain of video frames.
layer2.telemetry: Trajectory smoothness and identity switch rates.

primitives.name: Global Feature Attention Mechanism
primitives.verbatim_quote: Both query types benefit from self- and encoder-decoder attention on global frame-level features, thereby omitting any additional graph optimization or modeling of motion and/or appearance.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Attention Weight: dimensionless scalar summing to 1; Frame-level Features: high-dimensional tensor (dimensionless activations).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that global scene context contains sufficient discriminative information to resolve local ambiguities without hand-crafted motion heuristics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Degenerates in highly uniform scenes lacking distinct global features, causing attention heads to diffuse uniformly and lose target focus.

layer2.mapping: Directly mirrors GSI's use of global game-state tensors to update local player probabilities, bypassing traditional Kalman filtering.

primitives.name: Tracking-by-Attention Paradigm
primitives.verbatim_quote: TrackFormer introduces a new tracking-byattention paradigm and while simple in its design is able to achieve state-of-the-art performance on the task of multiobject tracking (MOT17 and MOT20) and segmentation (MOTS20).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Performance Metric: dimensionless score (e.g., MOTA); Segmentation Mask: binary spatial grid.
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that the attention mechanism inherently captures the complex dependencies required for both tracking and segmentation tasks.
primitives.breakdown_regime: May struggle with extremely fast-moving objects if the frame rate is too low to capture the attention shift effectively.

layer2.mapping: Forms the foundational kernel for GSE's real-time situational awareness, replacing heuristic tracking pipelines with pure attention-based inference.
layer2.telemetry: Overall benchmark rankings on MOT17/MOT20 datasets.

primitives.name: Track Identity Intersection
primitives.verbatim_quote: The two ground truth track identity sets describe a hard assignment of the Ntrack track query outputs to the ground truth objects in frame t: Kt ∩Kt-1: Match by track identity k.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Kt': 'Set of ground truth track identities at time t', 'Kt-1': 'Set of ground truth track identities at time t-1', 'Kt ∩ Kt-1': 'Intersection representing persistent tracks'}
primitives.assumptions: Tracks maintain identity across frames unless occluded or terminated.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When Kt ∩ Kt-1 = ∅, no persistent tracks exist between frames.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's belief update on track continuity; GSE's state transition from Kt-1 to Kt.
layer2.telemetry: Match rate of Kt ∩ Kt-1 vs. total tracks.

primitives.name: Track Occlusion Set
primitives.verbatim_quote: The second set of ground truth track identities Kt-1 \ Kt includes tracks which either have been occluded or left the scene at frame t.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Kt-1 \\ Kt': 'Set difference indicating occluded or exited tracks'}
primitives.assumptions: Occlusion or exit implies temporary or permanent disappearance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When Kt-1 \ Kt ≠ ∅, tracks are either occluded or terminated.

layer2.mapping: Derived kernel in GSE for background modeling; GSI computes probability of occlusion.
layer2.telemetry: Number of tracks in Kt-1 \ Kt per frame.

primitives.name: New Object Set
primitives.verbatim_quote: The last set Kobject = Kt \ Kt-1 of previously not yet tracked ground truth objects remains to be matched with the Nobject object queries.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Kobject': 'Set of newly appearing ground truth objects', 'Kt \\ Kt-1': 'Difference indicating new objects'}
primitives.assumptions: New objects must be matched with object queries via cost minimization.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When Kt \ Kt-1 ≠ ∅, new objects require assignment.

layer2.mapping: Kernel in GSE for novel object detection; GSI assigns likelihood to new object hypotheses.
layer2.telemetry: Assignment success rate of Kt \ Kt-1 to object queries.

primitives.name: Matching Cost Function
primitives.verbatim_quote: Given the ground truth class labels ci and predicted class probabilities ˆpi(ci) for output embeddings i, the matching cost Cmatch with class weighting λcls is defined as {\ca l C}_\text {matc h } = - \lambda _{\rm cls} \hat {p}_{\sigma (i)}(c_i) + {\cal C}_{\rm box}(b_{i}, \hat {b}_{\sigma (i)}).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C_match': 'Matching cost scalar', 'λ_cls': 'Class weight scalar', 'p̂_σ(i)(c_i)': 'Predicted class probability for true class', 'C_box': 'Box cost function (IoU or L1)', 'b_i, ŷ_σ(i)': 'Ground truth and predicted bounding boxes'}
primitives.assumptions: Cost function combines classification and localization error.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When class probabilities are near uniform, cost dominated by localization.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSI's loss landscape; GSE uses it for optimal query assignment.
layer2.telemetry: Mean cost value across all matched queries.

primitives.name: Deformable Transformer Encoder-Decoder
primitives.verbatim_quote: The Deformable DETR [71] encoder and decoder both apply 6 individual layers with multi-headed self-attention [51] with 8 attention heads.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'N': 'number of attention heads', 'L': 'number of transformer layers', 'C': 'channel dimension'}
primitives.assumptions: Multi-head self-attention operates on spatially deformed key-value pairs; each layer applies 8 attention heads across 6 stacked layers.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When spatial deformation exceeds learned receptive field, attention becomes ineffective.

layer2.mapping: The encoder-decoder structure maps spatio-temporal features to object-centric representations via cross-attention between frame features and track queries.
layer2.telemetry: Mean Average Precision (mAP) on MOT17 test set.

primitives.name: Bounding Box Refinement
primitives.verbatim_quote: Furthermore, we also apply the refinement of deformable reference point coined as bounding box refinement in [71].
primitives.assumptions: Reference points are updated iteratively based on predicted offsets from previous iteration.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If offset prediction diverges, refinement fails to converge to stable bounding boxes.

layer2.mapping: Refined reference points serve as kernel centers for dynamic bounding box regression during tracking.
layer2.telemetry: Intersection-over-Union (IoU) score improvement over baseline DETR.

primitives.name: Cost Function Weighting Parameters
primitives.verbatim_quote: The weighting parameters of the cost and their corresponding loss terms are set to λcls = 2, λl1 = 5 and λiou = 2.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'λ_cls': 'classification loss weight', 'λ_l1': 'L1 regression loss weight', 'λ_iou': 'IoU loss weight'}
primitives.assumptions: Loss components are combined linearly with fixed weights; optimal values determined empirically.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If λ_l1 is too low, localization errors dominate; if λ_cls is too high, classification accuracy suffers.

layer2.mapping: Weighted cost function defines objective landscape for optimizing object identity and position jointly.
layer2.telemetry: Tracking MOTA (Multiple Object Tracking Accuracy) performance metric.

primitives.name: Track Augmentation Probabilities
primitives.verbatim_quote: The probabilities for the track augmentation at training time are pFN = 0.4 and pFP = 0.1 Furthermore, every MOT17 [30] frame is jittered by 1% with respect to the original image size similar to the adjacent frame simulation.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_FN': 'probability of false negative augmentation', 'p_FP': 'probability of false positive augmentation'}
primitives.assumptions: Augmentation simulates real-world variability in object visibility and motion consistency.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Excessive augmentation may cause model confusion between true positives and augmented negatives.

layer2.mapping: Augmented training data enables robustness against missing or spurious detections in real-time tracking.
layer2.telemetry: Robustness measured by performance drop under noisy input conditions.

reasoning_traces.think: The derivation begins by recognizing that traditional multi-object tracking relies on a decoupled, two-step process: detection followed by heuristic association (e.g., Hungarian algorithm on IoU). TrackFormer fundamentally disrupts this by casting the entire problem as a single, differentiable set prediction task. Mathematically, this implies that the mapping from a video sequence to a set of trajectories is not a composition of disjoint functions, but a unified operator $\mathcal{F}: V \rightarrow \mathcal{T}$. The core innovation lies in the introduction of 'track queries,' which serve as persistent latent variables representing individual entities. Unlike static object queries used in DETR for initialization, track queries evolve autoregressively. This evolution is driven entirely by attention mechanisms interacting with global frame-level features extracted by a CNN backbone. From a mathematical physics perspective, the track query can be viewed as a state vector undergoing continuous transformation on a high-dimensional manifold defined by the attention weights. The absence of explicit motion or appearance models suggests that the attention mechanism implicitly learns a complex, non-linear dynamical system governing object persistence. This aligns perfectly with the Foundry Sovereign Primitives' goal of identifying minimal, powerful operators. The 'tracking-by-attention' paradigm essentially replaces rigid kinematic constraints with soft, data-driven probabilistic associations, allowing the model to handle occlusions and interactions more gracefully than traditional graph-based optimizers. The epistemic trace thus highlights a shift from rule-based state transitions to learned, attention-mediated state propagation.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive traces its lineage back to the foundational Transformer architecture introduced by Vaswani et al., which demonstrated the power of self-attention in sequence modeling. It specifically inherits from DETR (Carion et al.), which first applied Transformers to object detection by framing it as set prediction. TrackFormer extends this by adding a temporal dimension, creating a direct genealogical link between static image understanding and dynamic video analysis, ultimately bridging computer vision with sequential decision-making frameworks.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: In the context of Galaxy Sports Intelligence, the 'theory of mind' involves modeling the opposing agents—players, coaches, and even the ball—as entities possessing hidden intentions and trajectories. TrackFormer's ability to maintain identity through attention mimics a cognitive process of focusing on specific actors amidst a crowded field. By treating each player as a 'track query,' the system implicitly reasons about their roles and future positions based on global context, much like a coach anticipates plays. This allows GSE to predict not just where a player is, but who they are in the context of the unfolding game strategy.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition arises if the attention mechanism becomes overly diffused, failing to distinguish between similar-looking players in tight clusters. If the global frame features lack sufficient discriminative power (e.g., identical uniforms), the isomorphism between track queries and physical identities breaks down, leading to identity switches. Furthermore, if the autoregressive assumption fails due to sudden, unpredictable changes in player behavior (e.g., a feint), the model's reliance on past states may cause lag. Therefore, a cross-layer veto must be implemented to detect high-entropy attention maps or rapid divergence in predicted vs. actual trajectories, triggering a fallback to more robust, albeit slower, geometric verification methods.

It defines how track identities evolve over time through set operations: intersection Kt ∩ Kt-1 for persistent tracks, difference Kt-1 \ Kt for occlusions/exit, and Kt \ Kt-1 for new objects. These sets form the basis for hard assignment and cost-based matching. The matching cost function integrates classification and localization errors, enabling optimal query-to-ground-truth alignment. This formulation underpins both GSI’s probabilistic inference and GSE’s state transition logic. The combinatorial optimization approach ensures global consistency across frames. The derived primitives reflect the interplay between identity preservation, object emergence, and spatial localization in MOT systems. The inclusion of bounding box refinement ensures precise localization, while carefully tuned cost function weights balance classification and regression tasks. Training strategies such as track augmentation and frame jittering enhance generalization. These elements collectively form a coherent system where spatial-temporal context is encoded through attention, refined via iterative updates, and optimized via weighted losses. The empirical results in Tables A.1 and A.2 demonstrate superior performance compared to prior methods, particularly when handling public detection filtering via center distance or IoU thresholds. This suggests that the design choices support both strong tracking accuracy and robustness to imperfect inputs.
